data.narrative:
Reliable Robotics, a Series C-stage aerospace company founded by Robert Rose and Juerg Frefel, has raised $300M+ to date. The valuation analysis draws from a comp universe of 6 private-stage peers in Space & Aerospace (Sierra Space, Apex Space, Cowboy Space Corporation, Varda Space Industries, Aalyria, and one additional peer), supplemented by reference to 5 public comps (RKLB, PL, LUNR, ASTS, SATL) and a broader private peer set including SpaceX and Rocket Lab.

Two triangulation methods apply. Stage-progression analysis, using the $300M total raised as a proxy base and applying a typical 1.7x Series C step-up multiplier, implies a valuation of $510M. Peer-median analysis across the 6 same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables yields a median valuation of $1.8B, with a range of $1.1B to $8.0B. Public-comp anchoring cannot be applied given absence of target revenue data. The peer cohort spans wide dispersion, reflecting heterogeneous scale and stage maturity within frontier aerospace.

Triangulating these two applicable methods produces a valuation range of $434M (low) to $2.1B (high), with a median of $1.1B. Stage-progression suggests the lower bound; peer medians anchor the midpoint and upper range. Key uncertainties include (1) Reliable Robotics' current revenue and profitability trajectory relative to the peer set, (2) differentiation within the fragmented aerospace subsector, and (3) nearness to Series D or growth-stage milestones that would justify higher multiples.
